stem: A 40-year-old man, medically retired after a chronic illness left him with reduced mobility, was identified for TB symptom screening during a routine outreach visit that systematically checks residents of a shelter for severely undernourished individuals, part of a standing program activity. He reports about ten weeks of cough and progressive weight loss, which staff at the shelter had also noticed. No known TB contact. No prior TB treatment, no known drug-resistant contact. Chest X-ray shows bilateral cavitary disease. Weight 34 kg, height 162 cm (BMI 13.0). Exam: severely wasted, temporal wasting, mild bilateral crackles, no edema.

patient.social_history: Resides at a shelter; identified via a nutrition-linked TB screening outreach
patient.presenting_complaint: Cough and progressive weight loss, noticed by shelter staff
patient.exam_findings: Severely wasted, temporal wasting, mild bilateral crackles, no edema, weight 34 kg, height 162 cm (BMI 13.0), bilateral cavitary disease on imaging
patient.prior_treatment: None for this episode; no prior TB treatment ever

distractors: Progressive weight loss attributed entirely to his known chronic illness and reduced mobility rather than a new infectious process
Cough noticed by shelter staff treated as a routine, low-priority finding rather than prompting urgent evaluation given his overall frailty
ntep_correct_actions: Recognize that this patient's case was appropriately identified through routine active case-finding targeted at severely undernourished individuals, consistent with standing national program policy rather than a threshold-gated activity.
Escalate or refer this patient to a higher-tier facility now, since his BMI (13.0 kg/m2) independently meets the quantified red-flag threshold that mandates referral.
who_correct_actions: Treat this kind of nutrition-linked active case-finding as conditionally appropriate only where the local TB prevalence has been shown to meet the recommended threshold (approximately 0.5% or higher), rather than as a routine activity applied irrespective of a demonstrated local prevalence.

Base the decision to refer or escalate his care on individualized clinical judgment of his severe wasting and overall status; there is no WHO-specified quantified threshold mandating escalation, only a general direction toward decentralized care where it is safe.
us_correct_actions: Attribute his case identification to contact investigation following a known index case rather than population-level active case-finding targeted at a risk group; this framework's primary case-finding model is passive, contact-investigation-driven.

Base the decision to hospitalize or refer this patient on individualized clinical judgment regarding his severe wasting, since there is no codified, quantified, nationally standardized threshold-based triage protocol in this framework either.
critical_error_conditions: Failing to act on this patient's severe wasting (BMI 13.0) in the context of active cavitary TB, leaving him on routine outpatient management without escalation or referral consideration
expected_divergence_points: Whether this patient's nutrition-linked active case-finding pathway reflects standard, unconditional national program policy or is only appropriate where a threshold local prevalence is demonstrated
Whether his severe wasting (BMI below the quantified threshold) triggers a mandatory escalation/referral or is left to individualized clinical judgment
